newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries narrowly mixed in Tokyo before CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries narrowly mixed in Tokyo before CPI.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady to easier by Tokyo midday on Tuesday, with light speculative sales slightly depressing longer-end prices amid the recent bearish market trend, traders said.
Activity was dull as operators were waiting for the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) due at 1230 GMT, traders said.
"The market carried over the overnight sluggishness. Light speculative sales were spotted, but traders were unwilling to trade aggressively ahead of the CPI data," a bank trader said.
Economists polled by Reuters expected, on average, a rise of 0.2 percent in the overall CPI and 0.3 percent in the core.
The key 30-year bond stood at 93-7/32, yielding 7.18 percent, compared with 93-10/32 in New York on Monday.
The June T-bond futures contract fell 2/32 from the previous close to 106-20/32.
Traders said lingering credit-tightening concerns may push shorter-end yields higher, but bargain-hunting should emerge if the key bond yield rises above 7.2 percent.

"The yield curve may flatten further if rate hike fears grow even more," the trader said. "Operators have been holding back from active purchases, but they may start buying if the key bond yield rises to a level between 7.2 and 7.3 percent."
